title: Domain-adaptive diabetes prediction across heterogeneous cohorts
methods: Transfer learning; domain adaptation; multi-dataset validation; AUROC / calibration
datasets: Pima Indians Diabetes; NHANES; UCI diabetes; external hospital cohorts
findings: Single-cohort models drop substantially in AUROC on external populations; domain-adaptive training recovers part of the gap.
limitations: Limited South-Asian and low-resource cohorts; few studies report calibration by subgroup.
future_directions: Population-aware domain adaptation; cross-dataset AUROC and calibration reporting standards.
problem_statement: How can diabetes prediction models maintain reliable performance across different populations and datasets?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop a domain-adaptive ML model trained and validated across multiple independent diabetes datasets.

title: Early risk stratification for incident type 2 diabetes
methods: Explainable gradient boosting; demographic + lifestyle + biochemical features; SHAP
datasets: Prospective cohort studies; NHANES; primary-care EHR extracts
findings: Models can flag high-risk individuals years before clinical diagnosis when lifestyle and labs are available.
limitations: Missing labs common in primary care; limited validation in young adults.
future_directions: Early-stage risk models with transparent feature attributions for prevention programs.
problem_statement: How can AI identify individuals at high risk of developing diabetes before clinical diagnosis?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop an explainable ML model using demographic, lifestyle, clinical and biochemical features for early risk prediction.

title: Robust diabetes prediction under missing clinical parameters
methods: Median/MICE imputation; HistGradientBoosting; missingness indicators; sensitivity analysis
findings: Imputation + tree models preserve useful discrimination when key labs are missing at random.
limitations: MNAR missingness and systematic bias still degrade performance; few open benchmarks.
future_directions: Missing-data-robust pipelines with explicit uncertainty flags for clinicians and researchers.
problem_statement: How can diabetes prediction remain accurate when important clinical or laboratory parameters are missing?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop an ML model using missing-data imputation and robust feature-learning techniques.

title: Personalized treatment-response prediction in type 2 diabetes
methods: Treatment-outcome modeling; patient-level features; causal / quasi-experimental designs
datasets: Trial and observational treatment registries; EHR outcomes
findings: Heterogeneity of response to metformin, SGLT2i, GLP-1RA suggests room for individualized ranking of strategies.
limitations: Confounding by indication; limited genetic and adherence data.
future_directions: Personalized treatment-response models with clear uncertainty and external validation.
problem_statement: How can AI predict which treatment strategy may be more effective for an individual patient?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop a personalized treatment-response prediction model using patient characteristics, clinical history and treatment outcomes.

title: Multi-task prediction of diabetes complications
methods: Multi-task learning; nephropathy, retinopathy, CVD risk heads; shared representation
findings: Shared representations improve rare-complication detection versus independent models in some cohorts.
limitations: Label noise; unequal follow-up; under-representation of certain ethnic groups.
future_directions: Early multi-task complication risk tools with population-specific calibration.
problem_statement: How can AI predict the risk of developing diabetes-related complications at an early stage?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop multi-task ML models to predict complications such as nephropathy, retinopathy and cardiovascular risk.

title: Explainable AI for diabetes diagnosis and risk scoring
methods: SHAP; feature attribution; clinician-facing visualizations; biomarker ranking
datasets: Public diabetes tables; hospital laboratory panels
findings: Explanations increase trust and error-spotting when top features align with clinical knowledge.
limitations: Explanations can be unstable under correlated features; not a substitute for clinical judgment.
future_directions: Standardized explainable frameworks for diabetes ML with audit-ready reports.
problem_statement: How can diabetes prediction models provide clinically understandable explanations for their predictions?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop an explainable AI framework that identifies and visualizes the most influential biomarkers and clinical features.

title: Multimodal fusion for diabetes prediction
methods: Late/early fusion; clinical + lifestyle + imaging (retinal) + biomarkers
datasets: Multimodal research cohorts; retinal + tabular pairs
findings: Adding imaging or rich lifestyle signals can improve discrimination beyond labs alone in specialized settings.
limitations: Data alignment cost; missing modalities at inference; privacy of images.
future_directions: Practical multimodal pipelines that degrade gracefully when modalities are absent.
problem_statement: How can information from clinical records, biomarkers, lifestyle data and medical images be integrated for improved diabetes prediction?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop a multimodal AI model that combines heterogeneous biomedical data sources for disease prediction.

title: Population-aware diabetes risk models
methods: Stratified training; demographic/environmental features; external validation by ancestry or region
datasets: ICMR-INDIAB-style targets; multi-ethnic biobanks; regional EHR
findings: Models trained on one population often miscalibrate on another; population-aware features and recalibration help.
limitations: Sparse open South-Asian labeled datasets for deep models.
future_directions: Open population-aware benchmarks and domain-adaptive training recipes.
problem_statement: How can AI models account for differences in genetic, environmental and lifestyle factors across populations?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop population-aware ML models using demographic, environmental and clinical features and evaluate their generalizability.

title: AI-driven biomarker combination discovery for diabetes
methods: Feature selection; clustering; multivariate biomarker panels; stability selection
findings: Combinations of routine and novel markers can outperform single-marker rules for early risk strata in discovery cohorts.
limitations: Replication failure common; cost of novel assays.
future_directions: Reproducible biomarker-panel discovery with external validation and cost-aware selection.
problem_statement: How can AI identify combinations of biomarkers that may improve early detection and disease-risk stratification?
proposed_ai_solution: Apply feature selection, clustering and machine-learning techniques to discover potentially informative biomarker combinations.

title: NLP literature mining for diabetes research-gap discovery
methods: Abstract chunking; embedding retrieval; LLM extraction of methods, datasets, limitations, future work
datasets: PubMed diabetes abstracts; curated review sets
findings: Automated extraction surfaces recurring limitations (cross-dataset gap, missing data, weak explainability) faster than manual review.
limitations: Hallucination risk without grounding; citation accuracy must be audited.
future_directions: Grounded RAG systems that output evidence-based problem statements with citations.
problem_statement: How can AI analyse multiple diabetes research papers to identify recurring limitations, unexplored combinations and emerging research gaps?
proposed_ai_solution: Develop an NLP-based literature-mining system that extracts methods, datasets, findings, limitations and future directions from papers and generates evidence-based research problems.
